common.olderSnapshot: This snapshot is from analysis revision {revision}; this needs revision {needed} or later. Scan again to see it.

map.note: Ordered by how many other components use each unit, then how many units do. Rank is PageRank over who uses whom (members counted for their type, tests left out); 1 is the average unit.
map.paramLimit: How many units, most leaned-on first (default 40, at most 150).
map.paramOf: Only units in this component or area. Leave out for the whole codebase.
map.row: {i}. {name}: {signature} ({at}). Used by {usedBy} units in {usedByComponents} other components.{members}
map.summary: The units the rest of the code leans on most, with their signatures and most used members: a map of the codebase that fits in a few hundred lines.
map.title: The units the code leans on most
map.total: The {shown} units the rest of the code leans on most{of}, of {ranked} ranked.

entries.none: No entry points were found: no route, page, consumer, schedule, command or main written in a way this scan reads.
entries.paramFind: Text in the route, handler or unit, such as "/orders".
entries.paramKind: Which kind: http, page, message, event, schedule, cli, main, job, or all (default).
entries.paramOf: Only those handled in this component or area.
entries.summary: The ways into the code: HTTP routes, pages, consumed messages and events, schedules, commands and programs, with what handles each.
entries.title: Entry points
entries.unknownHandler: a handler the scan could not name

trace.also: Also matched: {list}. Ask for one by its full route or name.
trace.bound: {iface} leads on to {impl} in {component}, bound by {mechanism}.
trace.cut: The trace stops at {count} units; ask for fewer steps to see the nearest ones only.
trace.noData: No unit on this trace reads or writes stored data that the scan saw.
trace.noStart: No entry point or unit matches "{from}".
trace.order: Components in the order the trace reaches them: {list}.
trace.paramDepth: How many steps to follow (default 5, at most 8).
trace.paramFrom: Where to start: a route ("GET /orders/:id" or "/orders"), a handler, a command, or a unit by name.
trace.static: The trace follows imports and bindings. A call made by reflection, by a name in a string, or through an event is not seen.
trace.summary: The slice of the codebase one use case runs on: from an entry point or unit, what it uses step by step, through interfaces to their implementations, down to the data it reads and writes.
trace.title: What {from} runs on
trace.total: From {from}, the code reaches {units} units in {components} components within {depth} steps.

data.nothingNamed: No entity, table or component matches "{of}".
data.paramOf: An entity or table, to see who touches it; or a component, to see what it touches. Leave out for what is shared most widely.

shared.one: 1 of them is touched by more than one component.
shared.other: {count} of them are touched by more than one component.

data.summary: What the code stores and who touches it: entities and tables, which components read and write each, and which are shared.
data.title: Stored data and who touches it
data.total: The code stores {stored} things: {entities} declared as entities, {tables} named only as tables in SQL.

surface.caveat: Used means imported by name. A unit used only by reflection, a string or a framework convention looks unused here.

framework.one: 1 unit is reached by the framework rather than by imports (an entry point or a bound implementation): {list}.
framework.other: {count} units are reached by the framework rather than by imports (entry points or bound implementations): {list}.

inside.one: 1 unit is used only inside: {list}. It could be kept internal.
inside.other: {count} units are used only inside: {list}. They could be kept internal.

surface.noUnits: {of} declares no units this scan could read.
surface.summary: What a component really exposes: which of its units other components use, and by whom, against those used only inside it.

testsOnly.one: 1 unit is used from outside only by tests: {list}.
testsOnly.other: {count} units are used from outside only by tests: {list}.

surface.title: What {of} exposes
surface.total: {of} has {units} units: {exposed} used by other components ({components} of them), {inside} used only inside, {framework} reached by the framework.

bypass.one: 1 unit outside its own component uses {impl} directly instead of {name}: {list}.
bypass.other: {count} units outside its own component use {impl} directly instead of {name}: {list}.

implementations.noWiring: No container binding names {name}: its implementations are chosen in code, or by something this scan does not read.
implementations.paramOf: A type, usually an interface: by name, or by its full name when names repeat.
implementations.summary: What implements a type, where a container wires each implementation, and who uses an implementation directly instead of the type.
implementations.title: Implementations of {of}

origins.atHead: This file's repository is not the one the scan's commit belongs to, so its lines were dated at that repository's newest commit.
origins.capped: Only {dated} of the {files} files were dated; the rest are counted, not dated.
origins.closed: The cycle closed on {date}, when {from} started importing {to}: commit {commit} "{summary}" by {author}.
origins.cycle: The two are in the cycle {list}.

files.one: 1 file in {from} imports {to} today; {recent} of the {dated} dated started in the last year.
files.other: {count} files in {from} import {to} today; {recent} of the {dated} dated started in the last year.

origins.lastWrote: A line is dated by the commit that last wrote it: an import rewritten later (a move, a reformat) dates from the rewrite, so a date here is the latest the dependency can have started.
origins.latest: The newest file to start importing it: {file}, on {date} (commit {commit}, "{summary}", by {author}).
origins.noGit: Git is not reachable for this snapshot: its workspace folder is not a git checkout here.
origins.noSnippets: This snapshot does not keep where each import is written, so its imports cannot be dated.
origins.since: {from} has imported {to} since {date}: commit {commit} "{summary}" by {author}, in {file}.
origins.summary: When and why one component started importing another: the commit behind the oldest import still in place, the newest, and for a cycle, the commit that closed it.
origins.title: When {from} started importing {to}
origins.undated: {files} files in {from} import {to}, but git could not date their imports.

docs.none: This codebase has no documents: no README, decision record or guide.
docs.noneAbout: No document is about {of}: none sits in its folder, names its files or names its types.
docs.paramOf: A component, to see the documents about it. Leave out for every document.
docs.read: To read one, ask for the code of its file.
docs.summary: The written intent: decision records, architecture notes, READMEs and guides, and which code each is about.
docs.title: Documents

conventions.data: Stored data is touched from {area}: {share} of {total} places.{elsewhere}
conventions.declare: These are readings of what the code does, not rules anyone declared. A rule worth keeping can be declared in Rules, so a later scan says when it breaks.
conventions.heldPair: {lower} never imports {upper} ({references} references the other way)

kept.one: {lower} does not import {upper}, kept by {share} of {references} import references between them; 1 exception: {list}.
kept.other: {lower} does not import {upper}, kept by {share} of {references} import references between them; {count} exceptions: {list}.

conventions.none: Between these areas, no direction is kept by 90% or more of at least 10 import references.
conventions.oneArea: There is only one area here, so there are no directions between areas to read.
conventions.paramOf: Only the areas inside this component or area. Leave out for the whole codebase.
conventions.summary: The rules the code keeps without having declared them: which way imports run between areas, and where data and entry points live, with the exceptions.
conventions.title: Rules the code keeps
conventions.total: Between its {areas} areas, the code keeps {held} directions without exception and {kept} more with a few exceptions.

surprises.grain: {from} imports {to} ({file}), although {lower} otherwise never imports {upper}: one of the few of {references} import references between them that run that way.
surprises.hidden: {a} and {b} changed together in {commits} commits, but neither imports the other, directly or through anything else.
surprises.hub: {name} in {component} is used from {count} of the {of} components ({users} units in all).
surprises.none: Nothing stands out against this codebase's own norms. Looked at: {list}.
surprises.size: {name} has {lines} lines, {times} times the median of the {siblings} other components in {area}.
surprises.summary: What is unusual here against this codebase's own norms, each with its evidence.
surprises.title: What stands out
surprises.young: {name} is {days} days old but already used by {dependents} components.

kinds.hub: units most of the system uses

notes.author: By
notes.noWorkspace: Notes belong to a workspace; this snapshot was opened on its own.
notes.none: No notes yet. A note keeps what was learned about part of the code for the next conversation.
notes.older: (written against commit {commit}; the code may have moved on)
notes.paramOf: A component, file, unit or table, to see the notes about it. Leave out for all.
notes.subject: About
notes.summary: What a person or Ask wrote down about parts of the codebase in earlier sessions.
notes.title: Notes
